# `js/prefer-iterator-zip`

**`Iterator.zip()` for a loop that indexes parallel arrays**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (the new loop reads every row before the body and initialises each iterator up front, and `Iterator.zip` is not in every runtime yet; the author accepts that) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/prefer-iterator-zip` |

## What it checks

A `for` loop with a block body, a `let` index starting at `0`, stepped by one (`i++`, `++i`, `i += 1`, `i = i + 1`) and bounded by the shortest of two or more arrays — `i < Math.min(a.length, b.length)` or `i < a.length && i < b.length`, either way round, the `Math.min` result also cached in the loop head or in a `const`/`let` just before the loop that nothing else reads — whose body only reads `a[i]`, `b[i]` for those distinct identifiers, is reported on its head. The suggestion is `for (const [x, y] of Iterator.zip([a, b]))` with each read replaced by its name (the singular of the array's name, made unique). Single-input bounds, callbacks that capture the index or an array, property chains, optional indexing, offsets, writes, any other use of the index or of an array, and a string or plain object bound are left alone; a comment inside what the fix would rewrite leaves the finding without an edit. Behaviour of eslint-plugin-unicorn v79.0.0 (read, not copied).

**Why:** Reading several arrays at one index says "walk them together" in a way the reader has to reconstruct; `Iterator.zip` says it and stops at the shortest by itself. No engine ships it yet, so check the runtime before applying the suggestion.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/prefer-iterator-zip" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/prefer-iterator-zip" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/prefer-iterator-zip" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/prefer-iterator-zip" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/prefer-iterator-zip" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/prefer-iterator-zip": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/prefer-iterator-zip: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/prefer-iterator-zip expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/prefer-iterator-zip --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/prefer-iterator-zip       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/prefer-iterator-zip  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>          # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
for (let index = 0; index < Math.min(names.length, scores.length); index++) {
  save(names[index], scores[index]);
}
```

#### Do

```js
for (const [name, score] of Iterator.zip([names, scores])) {
  save(name, score);
}
```

#### Fixed

```js
for (const [name, score] of Iterator.zip([names, scores])) {
  save(name, score);
}
```
